group_assessment.weighting: Primary mouse study from a glymphatic-transport group, peer reviewed with a published review file that records reviewers doubting the central causal claim. Weigh as a descriptive study of a three-drug blockade in one acute model, not as proof that glymphatic flow mediates seizure control.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: adult FVB/2J mice (sex stated only in the title, male), intrahippocampal kainic acid, a cocktail of prazosin 6, propranolol 6 and atipamezole 0.6 mg/kg i.p. against vehicle; random allocation is stated, blinding is not.
entries.snippet: The PPA mixture contained prazosin hydrochloride (6 mg/kg; Sigma Aldrich, Cat. P7791), propranolol hydrochloride (6 mg/kg; Tocris Bioscience, Cat. 0624), and atipamezole hydrochloride (0.6 mg/kg
entries.anchor: Methods, Treatment with pan-adrenergic inhibitor cocktail

entries.proposition: In the acute status epilepticus the blockade prolonged individual convulsive seizures and the interval between them and the duration of phase 1 without changing the number of seizures; the abstract speaks of reduced severity.
entries.snippet: PPA treatment significantly prolonged the duration of individual seizures, the interval between seizures, and the duration of phase 1, but not the total number of seizures during phase 1
entries.anchor: Results, Pan-adrenergic inhibition delays and shortens KA-induced status epilepticus

entries.proposition: Table 1 gives the acute numbers: seizure duration 115.0 against 204.2 s (P < 0.001), interval 8.2 against 20.3 min, and the total duration of phase 1 plus phase 2 26.1 against 19.9 h (P = 0.265, not significant).
entries.snippet: Duration of Phase 1 + Phase 226.1 ± 4.2 h19.9 ± 2.0 h0.265

entries.proposition: The Discussion states the major electrophysiological effect was a shortening of the period of abnormal activity, and a subheading asks why enhancing glymphatic flow shortens seizure duration, while Table 1 shows longer individual seizures and a non-significant change in total duration.
entries.snippet: The major electrophysiological effect of pan-adrenergic blockage after KA infusion was the shortening of the period of abnormal electrical activity
entries.anchor: Discussion, Why does seizure activity reduce glymphatic influx

entries.proposition: MORTALITY: three-day blockade starting at 5 minutes reduced death in the first ten days (12 mice per group); the chronic-phase comparisons are therefore among survivors of unequal survival.
entries.snippet: PPA significantly reduced KA-induced mortality rate during the first ten days post KA infusion as compared with KA-Veh mice (Fig. 2C).
entries.anchor: Results, Pan-adrenergic inhibition improves behavioral outcomes

entries.proposition: DELAYED DOSING: starting the cocktail at 30 h did not shorten seizures nor rescue body weight or mortality; at two months only the number of convulsive seizures differed, not maximal Racine score or seizure-free days.
entries.snippet: At two months, the KA-PPA (30 h) group had a significant reduction in the number of convulsive seizures, but no difference in maximal Racine scale and number of convulsive seizure-free days at two months

entries.proposition: A single dose in chronic epilepsy lowered seizures only for about six hours and not over twelve (supplementary figure S8), an acute drug effect rather than a changed disease.
entries.snippet: The numbers of convulsive seizures during the 12 h post-drug administration were comparable between PPA and Veh groups (Fig. S8)
entries.anchor: Results, A single dose of PPA administered at the chronic phase

entries.proposition: LOCUS: the glymphatic gain was not significant in the hippocampus, the region of the kainic acid focus; the authors attribute it to gliosis and to a tracer protocol not optimised for the hippocampus.
entries.snippet: even though we did not find significant glymphatic enhancement in the hippocampus (Fig. 5C,I)
entries.anchor: Discussion, Epileptogenesis and the partial rescue

entries.proposition: CAUSALITY: the cocktail blocks neuronal adrenoceptors directly; the authors say they cannot exclude that this contributes to the shortening of seizures, so the glymphatic mediation is an inference from correlation and the knockout.
entries.snippet: We cannot exclude the possibility that inhibition of neuronal NE receptors also contributes to the shortening of the seizure.
entries.anchor: Discussion, Why does seizure activity reduce glymphatic influx, last paragraph

entries.proposition: The aquaporin-4 knockout experiment uses another strain (C57BL/6, 6 months) from the FVB mice of the drug experiments; the authors note knockouts have adaptive changes and that four of five wild-type controls had no spontaneous seizures.
entries.snippet: we here observed that four of five wildtype mice did not exhibit spontaneous seizures during the four consecutive days of recording in the chronic phase
entries.anchor: Results, Aqp4 knockout aggravated KA-induced SE

entries.proposition: Adrenergic receptor subtypes have both pro- and anti-seizure effects according to the paper own literature summary, so a blanket "adrenergic" direction does not exist even in the introduction to the discussion.
entries.snippet: The author argued that all three major subtypes of adrenergic receptors had both anti- and pro-seizure effects
entries.anchor: Discussion, Pan-adrenergic inhibition reduces KA-induced status epilepticus

entries.proposition: A wording slip: the Discussion says the cocktail dampened astrogliosis and increased pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, while the Results state the pro-inflammatory cytokines were higher in the vehicle kainic acid group and the cocktail lowered one of them (G-CSF).
entries.snippet: PPA exerted a clear anti-inflammatory role by dampening astrogliosis and increasing pro-inflammatory cytokine levels after KA infusion
entries.anchor: Discussion, Epileptogenesis and the partial rescue

entries.proposition: Figure 2C survival curves (12 mice per group): about half of vehicle-treated kainic acid mice died by day 10 against about one in seven with the cocktail; read from the plot; Figure 2D shows chronic-phase differences in 6 against 7 surviving mice (seizure-free days not significant).
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 2 panel C Kaplan-Meier plot: Sham near 100 percent, KA-Veh falling to about 50 percent by day 10, KA-PPA about 85 percent; panel D four dot plots with n 6 and 7, asterisks on seizure numbers, duration and maximum Racine, ns on seizure-free days.
